news.headline: Sundarpur village in Sarlahi mourns 13 residents killed in the Makwanpur microbus crash on the way home for Chhath
news.why_it_matters: Chakraghatta Rural Municipality will pay Rs 50,000 to each bereaved family for funeral costs and closed offices and schools for a day of mourning.

news.headline: Madhesh Chief Minister Yadav faces a confidence vote on 14 November after two parties withdraw support
news.why_it_matters: The Province Assembly meets at 1 pm after CPN-UML and the Nepali Communist Party pulled out of the government, so the province's leadership could change.

news.headline: Residents of Chhangru and Tinkar in Darchula leave their villages each November and return in April
news.why_it_matters: About 1,200 people from 199 households walk for around a week to lower areas such as Khalanga to escape heavy snow, and landslides have damaged sections of the trail.

news.headline: Karnali sets trials for 14 sports from 13 to 20 November ahead of the National Games on 2 to 13 December
news.why_it_matters: Selection trials run in Surkhet and Nepalgunj, and athletes in 31 disciplines are already in closed-camp training for the games hosted in the province.

news.headline: Plot subdivision stays suspended in 333 local units as only 420 of 753 have finished land classification
news.why_it_matters: The government is preparing a fourth amendment to the land use rules to let transactions resume where classification is incomplete, and each local unit needs at least Rs 1.5 to 2 million to finish the work.

news.headline: NEPSE slips on its first trading day after Tihar, with turnover of about Rs 3.05 billion
news.why_it_matters: The index closed near 2,649, down about six points, after 160 companies fell and 109 rose; the market is shut on Monday for Chhath and reopens on Tuesday.

news.headline: Nepal Rastra Bank collects Rs 200 billion in 20-day deposits from banks to absorb excess liquidity
news.why_it_matters: Banks and financial institutions bid online with a minimum of Rs 10 crore, and the deposits are repaid with interest on 17 Mangsir.

news.headline: Forty-two entities owe Kathmandu's airport more than Rs 1.55 billion, led by the airport customs office at Rs 572 million
news.why_it_matters: Himalaya Airlines owes Rs 357.7 million and Radisson's operator Rs 206.6 million, and the three together make up about 73% of the total.

news.headline: Lukla airport handles about 400 flights a day, including helicopters, as the trekking season picks up
news.why_it_matters: Three airlines run scheduled flights and six helicopter companies operate regularly, but the report gives no visitor counts.

news.headline: Only a handful of Nepali business groups employ more than 10,000 people after 35 years of liberalisation
news.why_it_matters: About 500,000 young people join the labour market each year, and the article blames weak capital spending, policy uncertainty and slow private credit growth of roughly 5 to 6%.

news.headline: Indian children cross the border daily to study in Nepali schools in Jhapa, Bardiya, Rautahat and Birgunj
news.why_it_matters: In Birgunj alone, Gyanada Academy takes about 100 pupils a day from Raxaul and nearby villages, with families citing teacher shortages and irregular classes on the Indian side.

news.headline: Foreign Minister Khanal asks COP31 for early warning systems built for mountains, with shared cross-border river data
news.why_it_matters: He also wants grant-based climate finance and alerts in local languages after the 26 August floods, saying the millions of text messages Nepal sent were not enough.

news.headline: The Gachhe-Bhalubang road, 73 km long, is being graveled and asphalted to cut the trip from 120 km by 47 km
news.why_it_matters: About 47.5 km of graveling between Gachhe and Lamatal is done, and paving is funded by Rs 100 million shared by the federal and provincial governments this fiscal year.

news.headline: NEPSE falls on reopening after Tihar, with turnover of Rs 3.05 billion across 335 companies
news.why_it_matters: Hydropower took the most turnover at about Rs 1.31 billion; Ghorahi Cement led single-stock turnover at Rs 400.7 million after dropping 7.87%.

news.headline: Central bank absorbs Rs 200 billion from banks for 20 days through online bidding
news.why_it_matters: The stated aim is to manage excess liquidity; the interest rate is set by the bids and the money is repaid on 17 Mangsir.

news.headline: Kathmandu airport has not collected over Rs 1.55 billion from 42 entities
news.why_it_matters: The airport customs office owes Rs 572 million and has not paid since 1999, while most airlines on the list other than Himalaya Airlines have stopped operating.

news.headline: Plot subdivision is suspended in 333 local units while the government drafts a fourth land use amendment
news.why_it_matters: Only 420 of 753 local units have classified their land, so buyers and developers in the rest cannot split plots.

news.headline: Few Nepali groups employ over 10,000 people; IME Group cites about 20,000 staff
news.why_it_matters: Chaudhary, Triveni and Shankar groups each report about 15,000, while 500,000 young people enter the labour market a year.

news.headline: Foodgrain imports via Birgunj fall about 64% to 31,640,000 kg in the quarter to 17 October
news.why_it_matters: Rice imports were Rs 898.1 million for 6,773,629 kg, while paddy fell from Rs 1.462 billion to Rs 333.5 million.

news.headline: FNCCI and IME Group invite UAE investors to hydropower, tourism, agriculture, IT and data centres
news.why_it_matters: The talks in Dubai ran alongside the RAK Investment Summit-2026 and also proposed direct flights to Bhairahawa.

news.headline: Pokhara tax office collects Rs 1.715 billion against a Rs 1.512 billion target in the 17 September to 17 October period
news.why_it_matters: That is about 13% above target, with income tax at Rs 1.088 billion against Rs 794.4 million, though VAT fell 15% short.

news.headline: Nawalparasi registers 204 new enterprises in 3.5 months but cancels 173
news.why_it_matters: The new ones are 92 industrial and 112 commercial; 62 industrial and 111 commercial registrations were cancelled, while over 6,800 businesses remain active.

news.headline: Lukla airport runs about 400 flights a day as the trekking season picks up
news.why_it_matters: Tara Air, Summit Air and Sita Air fly scheduled services, and six helicopter companies operate regularly.

news.headline: Insurance regulator resolves 312 complaints in nine months, 299 cases still pending
news.why_it_matters: Of those, 241 ended in formal verdicts and 71 in mutual settlement; 94 more were processed in the first trimester of FY 2026/27.

opportunities.title: 11th Nepal International Trade Fair
opportunities.detail: Held 18 to 22 November in Kathmandu with more than 200 stalls focused on cardamom, tea, ginger, handicrafts, pashmina and electric vehicle and domestic manufacturing pavilions; the report does not say how to book a stall.

opportunities.title: Koshi concessional loans for youth businesses
opportunities.who: Young people running small and medium enterprises in Koshi Province
opportunities.detail: The provincial government set aside Rs 8 billion in this year's budget for concessional loans over three years; the report gives no eligibility rules, application steps or deadline.

opportunities.title: Nepal Tourism Board Kukur Tihar reel contest
opportunities.who: Anyone able to make an English-language video; no limits are stated
opportunities.detail: The winner of the original video contest receives Rs 100,000; post the video on Instagram or Facebook with #NepalFestival and #KukurTihar and email it with a Drive link to the board.

The two in final review have since been approved: Kantipur Pharmaceuticals Lab (Nov 5, Rs 17 crore) and Aashutosh Energy (Nov 6, 1.2 million shares, Rs 12 crore). Added since (Nov 4): Tenx Hydro Holding, 800,000 shares worth Rs 8 crore.

watch.disclaimer: A rules-based screen built from published quarterly reports and the latest closing price. It is not investment advice, not an official rating and not a recommendation to buy or sell.
watch.method: Score out of 100: earnings yield (EPS / price) 35%, return on equity (EPS / book value) 30%, price-to-book, lower is better, 15%, and year-on-year profit growth 20%, each ranked against the other stocks in the list. Minus 15 if bad loans (NPL) are above 6%, minus 7 if 5-6%, minus 10 if distributable profit is negative. Screen leaders are the top three with no warning flags.
watch.universe: Listed banks that have published Q1 FY 2083/84 results so far. More companies are added as their quarterly reports come out.

invest.disclaimer: Projections apply fixed yearly rates and are not promises. Real returns vary year to year, and market options can lose money. This is general information, not investment advice; talk to a licensed adviser before investing.

inflation.note: Latest year-on-year inflation (mid-August to mid-September 2026). Last fiscal year averaged about 2.9%.

options.access: Locked for the term; breaking it early costs interest.
options.basis: Lowest (3.40%), average (4.01%) and highest (4.50%) published fixed deposit rates at commercial banks for Kartik 2083. Rates reset when the deposit renews.
options.name: Bank fixed deposit
options.tax_note: 6% tax is withheld on interest each year.

options.access: Sold only during government issue windows (minimum Rs 10,000); held to maturity.
options.basis: Fixed 6.5% coupon of the last issue (Rs 2.5 billion, five years), paid every six months. New issues may pay a different rate, and after 5 years the money is assumed to be reinvested at the same rate.
options.detail: Government of Nepal, 5-year Citizen Savings Bond-2087, last issue November to December 2025
options.name: Citizen savings bond
options.tax_note: Interest is taxed at source like deposit interest; 6% assumed.

options.access: Sold only during issue windows; eligibility rules apply.
options.basis: 7.5% coupon of the November to December 2025 issue (Rs 500 million), paid every six months. Only Nepalis in foreign employment, or recently returned, can buy, in their own or a family member's name.
options.detail: Government of Nepal, 5-year Foreign Employment Savings Bond-2087 for migrant workers and returnees
options.name: Foreign employment savings bond
options.tax_note: Tax treatment varies by issue; 6% assumed. Some issues have been tax-free.

options.access: Sell any trading day, but prices swing and can stay low for years.
options.basis: Low: no growth. Expected: 4.28% a year, the index's growth over the last 10 years (1,718 in mid-July 2016 to 2,648.89 on 13 Nov 2026). High: 8.69% a year, the long-run average over about 22 years. Price growth only; dividends would add to these figures, and some years lose money.
options.detail: A spread of listed shares that moves with the NEPSE index
options.name: NEPSE shares
options.tax_note: Capital gains tax 3.75% if held over 365 days, 5% otherwise (from 22 Sept 2026). Broker fees not included.

options.access: Sell any day at the dealer's buying rate.
options.basis: Assumed rates. Gold rose about 73% in 2025 (Rs 151,000 to Rs 261,000 a tola) and about 8% so far in 2026; it jumped Rs 13,300 on 5 Nov, fell Rs 5,900 on 6 Nov and ended the week Rs 2,700 higher. By 10 Nov it was Rs 284,300, up 17.72% in a year and Rs 55,000 below the Rs 339,300 record of 29 Jan. Spikes like 2025 rarely repeat, and gold can fall for years.
options.detail: Fine gold, Rs 284,300 a tola on 10 Nov 2026
options.name: Gold
options.tax_note: Tax not modeled. Making charges on jewellery and the dealer's buy-sell gap are not included.

options.access: Slow to sell; can take months, and prices vary plot by plot.
options.basis: Assumed rates. Nepal has no reliable land price index; the central bank stopped its price survey in 2022 because the data could not be trusted. Prices have fallen in slumps (about a third in Kathmandu Valley plots in 2012) and stalled in 2022-25, while deals recovered in 2025/26: transaction value rose to Rs 720.86 billion from Rs 386.15 billion. Rent is not included.
options.detail: A plot or house bought to hold and sell later
options.name: Land and property
options.tax_note: Capital gains tax 7.5% if held more than 5 years, 10% if 5 years or less (budget 2083/84). A 4% buying cost is assumed for the registration fee, which runs about 3-5.3% in Kathmandu Valley and is 25-30% lower for women buyers.

options.access: Slow to sell, and the building needs a manager and upkeep.
options.basis: Assumed: 60% of the money buys land, which grows at the land rates; 40% builds rooms or shops, held at what they cost to build. Rent after upkeep and empty months is assumed at 2%, 3% or 4% of the money put in each year, kept at the same rupee amount, and saved in a fixed deposit at the average rate. Check real rents nearby before relying on these.
options.detail: Land with rooms or shops built to rent out, such as student housing
options.name: Land plus rental building
options.tax_note: 10% local tax on rent; capital gains 7.5% if held more than 5 years, 10% otherwise, when sold.

places.note: Places where published data or big projects point to rising demand for land. Transaction figures count deals, not prices per plot. The outlook is Claude's reading of the drivers and risks, not a price forecast or advice; check local prices, title and access roads before buying.

drivers: Provincial capital with a new health sciences university in Geta, which got its first 90 seats, including 50 MBBS, in October 2026.
Irrigation expansion in Kailali, with Rs 1.33 billion of tenders out and more planned.
Rani Jamara Kulariya irrigation is about three-quarters built.
places.name: Dhangadhi
risks: The planned airport runway extension stalled and is under an anti-corruption investigation.
Sudurpashchim still has among the fewest property deals of any province.
places.signal: Property deals rose 73.16% in the April-July 2026 quarter, the fastest growth of any sub-metropolitan city.

drivers: Nepal and India are expected to mark the start of an integrated check post at Dodhara Chandani, and open a road bridge over the Mahakali, during PM Shah's India visit around 22 November 2026.

The four-lane Mahakali bridge and an 8 km six-lane access road are already built; the port's 42-hectare site will hold customs, quarantine, immigration and two warehouses, with a possible rail link to India.
The dry port would give a shorter trade route to Indian ports and north-east India, and could draw herbal and food processing industries.
Shuklaphanta National Park and the Mahakali corridor support tourism.
Land services are moving to every local government within a month, which should make registering plots in Bhimdatta simpler.
places.name: Bhimdatta and Dodhara Chandani
risks: Sudurpashchim has among the lowest property deal volumes in the country.
Plans for an industrial zone and the Mahakali corridor have moved slowly, and the Mahakali irrigation project is only about a quarter built.
Factories across Sudurpashchim run at only about half their capacity, and provincial growth was about 3.3% last year.
Plot subdivision has been frozen since mid-July in the 331 of 753 local governments that have not finished land use classification; check whether the municipality you buy in has.
places.signal: The India-funded dry port at Dodhara Chandani (about Rs 2.37 billion in Indian rupees) reached 26% completion by early November 2026, up from about 13% in June, on a 30-month schedule.

sources.name: Ratopati via Hamro Patro: 12.85% in June

drivers: People moving to the city keep pushing up demand for land.
Bagmati led every province in deals and declared value.
places.name: Kathmandu and Lalitpur
risks: Prices are the highest in the country, so the same budget buys far less land.
Valley plots fell about a third in the 2012 slump.
places.signal: Deals rose 155.74% in Kathmandu (value up 217.40%) and 136.92% in Lalitpur in the April-July 2026 quarter.

drivers: The regional international airport is technically complete.
Steady tourism; the Annapurna region drew nearly 33,000 foreign visitors in Ashoj.
places.name: Pokhara
risks: Airport traffic depends on airlines adding routes.
places.signal: Deals rose 108.71% in the April-July 2026 quarter.

drivers: Sits near the route of the Kathmandu-Terai Expressway, which is about 46% built with a target of mid-April 2027.
places.name: Hetauda
risks: The expressway is still being built, so the benefit depends on it finishing on time.
places.signal: Led all sub-metropolitan cities in land area traded (up 104.16%) and value (up 186.80%) in the April-July 2026 quarter.

drivers: A central crossroads city with growing deal activity.
places.name: Bharatpur
risks: Growth slower than Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Pokhara.
places.signal: Deals rose 63.04% in the April-July 2026 quarter.

drivers: The upgraded highway cuts the drive to Narayangadh to about two hours, linking Butwal faster to Chitwan and Kathmandu.
Gautam Buddha International Airport in nearby Bhairahawa is fully built, with a 3 km runway.
Officials plan a Buddhist tourism circuit linked to Lumbini and services for migrant workers from western Nepal.
places.name: Butwal
risks: The airport has had no scheduled international flights for more than six months; airlines cite too few passengers.
The road deadline has been extended four times, most recently to August 2026.
places.signal: The 114 km Narayangadh-Butwal road, widened to four to six lanes, was 81% built in April 2026, and its eastern section reached 92% by July. The central bank has not published city-level deal figures for Butwal; Lumbini is among the top three provinces for land area traded.

drivers: Main trade gateways to India; Birgunj handles almost half of Nepal's imports.
places.name: Biratnagar and Birgunj
risks: The Nijgadh international airport in Madhesh has not started.
places.signal: Deals rose 47.59% in Biratnagar and 29.19% in Birgunj; Madhesh was the only province where the number of deals fell (down 3.44%).
